The letter says the distribution is 'subject to Capital Market Authority approval'.
interim_dividend.evidence: PRIMARY SOURCE, fully decisive. du's own signed disclosure letter to DFM (Ref RME/14/2026, dated 22 July 2026, on du letterhead, addressed to DFM CEO Hamed Ahmed Ali, signed by Company Secretary Ali Al Ali and stamped by the eitc Chairman Office) carries an explicit bilingual three-column dividend timetable table: LED (last entitlement date) 30 July 2026 | EXD (ex-dividend date) 31 July 2026 | RCD (record closure date) 3 August 2026. Therefore DU went ex the AED 0.26 interim on FRIDAY 31 JULY 2026, which is SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS (six DFM trading sessions: 31 Jul, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 Aug) BEFORE the close on Friday 7 August 2026. At the 7 August 2026 close the AED 0.26 was NOT in the price - the shares had already traded ex for a week. The dividend was however still UNPAID at that date (payment 21 August 2026), so for valuation purposes it is a declared-but-unsettled distribution: out of the share price, still a liability on the balance sheet / a cash outflow yet to occur.
corroboration: DFM Dividends Distribution Summary row for DU: disclosure 22/07/2026, ex-dividend (T+1) 31/07/2026, settlement (T+2) 03/08/2026, 26 Fils, payment 21/08/2026. NOTE: the entitlement (T+0) cell in that DFM table reads 30/06/2026, which is internally inconsistent with an ex-date of 31/07/2026 under DFM's own T+0/T+1/T+2 convention (T+0 must be the trading day immediately before the ex-date). du's own letter gives LED = 30 July 2026, so the DFM summary cell is a month-digit data-entry slip (or is showing the 30 June 2026 period end); it does not affect the ex-date.
stockanalysis.com (DFM:DU) dividend history: Ex-Dividend Date Jul 31 2026, Record Date Aug 3 2026, Pay Date Aug 21 2026, 0.260 AED.

PRIOR-YEAR PATTERN CONFIRMS THE SHAPE: Dubai CSD Dividends Distribution Summary for the 2025 interim (24 Fils): entitlement (T+0) 31/07/2025 (Thu), ex-dividend (T+1) 01/08/2025 (Fri), settlement (T+2) 04/08/2025 (Mon), payment 22/08/2025 (Fri). The 2026 interim is the identical calendar structure shifted one day earlier: cum Thu 30 Jul, ex Fri 31 Jul, record Mon 3 Aug, pay Fri 21 Aug. (User's note of a 21 Aug 2025 payment is one day off the CSD record of 22 Aug 2025.)

FY2025 final (40 Fils) per DFM summary: entitlement 07/04/2026, ex-dividend 08/04/2026, settlement 09/04/2026, payment 29/04/2026 - i.e. the ex-date was 8 April 2026, and DFM records payment on 29 April 2026 (user's note said 28 April 2026, one day off). The 30 March 2026 AGM approval date is consistent.
interim_dividend.price_action_caveat: A mechanical ex-dividend drop is NOT visible in aggregator daily closes (stockanalysis: 30 Jul 12.20 -> 31 Jul 12.16, a -0.33% move, not the ~2.1% the AED 0.26 would imply; 7 Aug 2026 close 12.30). This does not undercut the ex-date, which is a documented matter of record in du's own filing: aggregator series may be dividend-adjusted, and in any case a stock can rise through its ex-date on market moves. Do NOT infer the ex-date from price action here - the filing governs. Note also that Monday 3 August 2026 is absent from that aggregator's price table despite being a DFM trading day, so treat its DU daily series as incomplete.
interim_dividend.valuation_implication: Any 7 August 2026 spot used as a valuation anchor is an EX-dividend price. Do not deduct the AED 0.26 from it again, and do not add it back as though the dividend were still in the price. If the model carries declared-but-unpaid dividends as a liability, the AED 0.26 (payable 21 August 2026) was still outstanding at the 7 August 2026 close.

royalty_extension.document_title: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company PJSC ("du") - Disclosure Announcement - Extension of Federal Royalty Scheme for the Period 2027-2029
royalty_extension.document_authenticity: du-branded standalone disclosure announcement (du logo, dateline 'Dubai, UAE - 24 July 2026'). PDF metadata: Microsoft Word, author 'Bisrat Marcos', CreationDate Fri 24 Jul 2026 14:02:28 UTC - i.e. the file was created on the date it carries, consistent with a company-issued release rather than a press rewrite. Read as a rendered image to confirm branding and wording.
royalty_extension.period: 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029 (a further three-year period)
royalty_extension.royalty_rate: 38% of net profits generated in the UAE
royalty_extension.corporate_tax_rate: 9% of net profits generated in the UAE after deduction of the Federal Royalty amount
royalty_extension.floor_treatment: CARRIES OVER - the AED 1.8 billion per year combined minimum floor is expressly retained in the extension, not lapsed. It is stated as an aggregate annual floor on Federal Royalty PLUS Corporate Tax combined (not royalty alone), the same construction as the 2024-2026 regime.
royalty_extension.payment_timing: Payable within five months from the end of the relevant fiscal year

quoted_words.extension: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company PJSC ("du" or the "Company"), listed on the Dubai Financial Market under ticker symbol DU, announces that it has been notified by the Ministry of Finance of the extension of the existing Federal Royalty regime and Corporate Tax Law applicable to the telecommunications sector for a further three-year period, commencing on 1 January 2027 and ending on 31 December 2029.
quoted_words.royalty_rate: A Federal Royalty rate of 38% shall apply to net profits generated in the UAE.
quoted_words.corporate_tax: A Corporate Tax rate of 9% shall apply to net profits generated in the UAE after deduction of the Federal Royalty amount.
quoted_words.floor: The aggregate annual amount of Federal Royalty and Corporate Tax payable by the Company shall not be lower than AED 1.8 billion.
quoted_words.payment_timing: The annual Federal Royalty and Corporate Tax amounts shall be payable within five months from the end of the relevant fiscal year.

exclusions_from_royalty_calculation: Profits generated by international controlled entities.
Profits generated by international non-controlled entities, including associates and joint ventures.
Dividends or other profit distributions received from international investments that are subject to local corporate tax, or a similar tax, in the relevant jurisdiction at a rate of 9% or above.
Profit attributable to non-controlling interest holders in UAE controlled entities.
